name: How much does a family-room addition cost per square foot in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget per square foot for a family-room addition in Los Angeles if I want a mid-range finish?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget per square foot for a family-room addition in Los Angeles if I want a mid-range finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic budget for a Los Angeles family-room addition depends on whether the project is a simple bump-out, a full rear addition, or part of a larger remodel. The biggest cost drivers are foundation requirements, roof tie-ins, framing, windows, electrical, HVAC extensions, and finish quality. In high-cost neighborhoods like Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, pricing can climb quickly when the addition must match an older home or meet stricter design expectations. Homeowners should ask for an all-in estimate that includes design, permits, utility work, and contingency, not just framing and drywall. A good comparison point is cost per square foot, but the number only makes sense when scope is clearly defined. The most useful quotes break out hard construction costs, design fees, and city-related fees separately.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most Los Angeles family-room additions fall in a broad per-square-foot range that changes with foundation work, structural upgrades, HVAC, and finish level. A mid-range project often costs more than a basic bump-out because family rooms usually need larger spans, better lighting, and seamless integration with the existing home.
